doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: Manuel Perez's playing and lessons
summary: De De recalls Manuel Perez as a powerful street trumpeter like Joe Nicholas, and says he got a few lessons at his house on Sundays.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, just part of them then, three children there. Yeah, we were nine. Well, let's see if I can think of anything else to ask you now. When you were a boy, D.D., do you remember the first parades you ever heard? What were they like? Even if you don't remember who the musicians were, how big a band?
In fact, always did like music. Swing it to me, huh? You know, I always did like jazz. Anywhere somebody was singing or playing, I would, you know, like in other words, like music.
Did you ever hear Manuel Perez's band?
Oh, yes, yes, yes. I don't remember the members, though. Oh yeah, I know him. I visited home. I visited home, intro his sons, you see? Yes.
How did he play? What style of trumpet?

Manuel was what we call a street man, powerful, strong. He was just like Joe Nicholas. They were what they called, powerful man behind the trumpet, and blow out loud, you know? That's right, that man was. He was a good musician. And music, and music, oh yeah, man. Great. And he started.
I guess he used to teach music quite a bit, I remember. Yeah, he did. He never took any lessons, though, from him.

He served several, like a few lessons, I'd go to the house like on Sundays with the kids, and we'd go over some music and stuff like that. Yeah, he taught me a little, you know. Yes, I understand. Yeah, yeah, I know him very well. The family, rather.
